previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, diabetes, and prior MSSA abscess was admitted for new bilateral leg swelling and exertional shortness of breath. The swelling began two days prior and was associated with a 20-pound weight gain, coinciding with an increase in gabapentin dose six days earlier. Workup revealed no pulmonary embolism, DVT, heart failure, or infection. The rash on his thighs was determined to be benign folliculitis, not vasculitis or cellulitis. Gabapentin was reduced to the prior dose, Lasix was given for fluid management, and compression stockings were started. Symptoms improved during the stay. He was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.

Complications: None.

1) Structure: Axial dual-inversion T1-weighted images of the myocardium were
obtained without spectral fat saturation pre-pulses in 5-mm contiguous slices.
2) Function: Breath-hold cine SSFP images were acquired in the left
ventricular 2-chamber, 4-chamber, horizontal long axis, short axis slices (8-
mm slices with 2-mm gaps), sagittal and coronal orientations of the left
ventricular outflow tract, and aortic valve short axis orientations.
3) Flow: Phase-contrast cine images were obtained transverse to the aorta
(axial plane) and main pulmonary artery (oblique plane).


Findings:
Structure and Function
There was normal epicardial fat distribution. The pericardial thickness was
normal. There were no pericardial or pleural effusions. The origins of the
left main and right coronary arteries were identified in their customary
positions.  The indexed diameters of the ascending and descending thoracic
aorta were normal.  The main pulmonary artery diameter index was mildly
dilated.  The left atrial AP dimension was normal.  The left and right atrial
lengths in the 4-chamber view were moderately enlarged.  The coronary sinus
diameter was normal.
The left ventricular end-diastolic dimension index was normal.  The end-
diastolic volume index was normal.  The calculated left ventricular ejection
fraction was normal at 56% with normal regional systolic function.  The
anteroseptal wall was mildly thickened and the inferolateral wall thickness
was normal. The left ventricular mass index was normal.  The right ventricular
end-diastolic volume index was normal.  The calculated right ventricular
ejection fraction was normal at 57%, with normal free wall motion.
The aortic valve appeared to open well but the number of leaflets could not be
determined.

Quantitative Flow
There was no significant intra-cardiac shunt.  Aortic flow demonstrated no
significant aortic regurgitation.  The calculated mitral valve regurgitant
fraction was consistent with no mitral regurgitation.   The resultant
effective forward LVEF was normal at 56%. The right ventricular stroke volume
and pulmonic flow demonstrated no significant pulmonic and no tricuspid
regurgitation.


Non-Cardiac Findings
There was extensive fat deposition, also seen on recent chest CT.

Impression:
1. Normal left ventricular cavity size with normal regional left ventricular
systolic function.  The LVEF was normal at 56%. The effective forward LVEF was
normal at 56%.
2. Normal right ventricular cavity size and systolic function. The RVEF was
normal at 57%.
3. The indexed diameters of the ascending and descending thoracic aorta were
normal. The main pulmonary artery diameter was mildly dilated, though normal
by index.
4. Bi-atrial enlargement.
5. A note is made of extensive abdominal, mediastinal and subcutaneous fat
deposition.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and color sonogram was performed on the right lower
extremity.  The right common femoral, superficial femoral and popliteal veins
are normal in compressibility, augmentation and Doppler waveforms.  The right
posterior tibial veins are compressible and patent.  The right peroneal veins
are not visualized.  There is, however, no evidence of deep vein thrombosis.

IMPRESSION:  Non-visualization of right peroneal veins, but otherwise no
evidence of deep vein thrombosis in the right lower extremity.
